newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices spiral down $7.00 per tonne.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices spiral down $7.00 per tonne.

text.p: Asia's high sulphur fuel oil spiralled downwards more than $7 per tonne in a market awash with supplies and no buyers, traders said on Tuesday.
"There are just no outlets for the unsold supplies," said a trader.
Late Tuesday, offers came down to $96, sharply lower compared with Monday's lowest offer of $103.
In the swaps market, prices fell more than $6.50 per tonne.
February was offered at $96.00, down from $104.50 on Monday.
February last traded at $97.50, while the February/March contango widened to $2.00 per tonne from $1.00 Monday.
Traders said a $1.00 spread traded, from 75 cents on Monday. By late Tuesday, only sellers were seen.
Traders said the usual term supplies from South Korea and Middle east were heading for Asia, which would add to an already oversupplied market.
Traders said more than 100,000 tonnes of fuel oil was overhanging the Singapore prompt market.
Adding to the woes of sellers, stocks were also high in Europe and prices soft, cutting the arbitrage to Europe.
Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) tender to sell high sulphur fuel oil, which closed Monday, is due to be awarded Wednesday, company officials said.
Traders said they heard the highest bid was at $101 per tonne, which represented a fall of $20 compared with its last tender for January loading supplies.
CPC last sold two cargoes of 30,000 tonnes each to a Singapore trader for January 11-30 loading supplies at $121-$1222 a tonne.
